verses.text: In that day you will say, “I will give thanks to you, Yahweh; for though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away and you comfort me.
Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust, and will not be afraid; for Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.”
Therefore with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.
In that day you will say, “Give thanks to Yahweh! Call on his name. Declare his doings among the peoples. Proclaim that his name is exalted!
Sing to Yahweh, for he has done excellent things! Let this be known in all the earth!
Cry aloud and shout, you inhabitant of Zion; for the Holy One of Israel is great among you!”

footnotes.content: Listen to the shift in 'that day'—from judgment turned to comfort. The people move from bearing anger to offering gratitude in a single breath. I've learned this too: the way to joy often runs straight through the acknowledgment of God's mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When Isaiah anchors salvation in Yah himself, he names trust as the antidote to fear—not as absence of dread, but as turning toward the One who is both strength and song. To rest there is to find what the world cannot shake.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Drawing water from wells of salvation—imagine the concrete joy of that image: coming to a spring-source that runs deep and never fails. The labor of drawing is part of the gladness; we don't receive passively, but reach toward our help with our own hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The testimony overflows into proclamation: give thanks, call His name, declare His doings to the peoples. Gratitude becomes a herald's work—not something private, but meant to be told wherever there are ears to hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Singing rises from excellence—the deeds God has done are excellent, and song is the fitting answer. Let it be known in all the earth: this invitation includes us. Our small voice joins His great work, and that union itself is reason to sing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cry rings out: the Holy One of Israel is great among you. Readers today hear an echo in that address—an invitation to inhabitants of Zion, whether ancient Jerusalem or the household of faith now. His greatness dwells not in the distant, but among those who belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
